summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines admits most nationalities visa-free: visitors from the UK, the US and the Schengen countries are granted up to six months on arrival and most others up to three months, extendable at the Immigration Department. CARICOM nationals get up to six months and OECS nationals an indefinite stay, while ten nationalities must apply to the Ministry of National Security for a visa in advance.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date you arrive.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — St Vincent and the Grenadines entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. WHO's country list gives the requirement for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — St Vincent and the Grenadines entry requirements

alsoStatedOn.name: WHO — International Travel and Health, country list: vaccination requirements and WHO recommendations (2022)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

onwardTicket.text: No official Vincentian source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask you to show a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for visa-free visitors to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask for proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay. Nationals who need an entry visa must include a financial statement with their visa application to the Ministry of National Security.

payments.text: No official source we checked describes card acceptance. Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted alongside the East Caribbean dollar, and the UK government says taxi fares can often be paid in US dollars — agree the fare with the driver before you set off.

safety.text: Most visits are trouble-free, but the UK Foreign Office reports crimes including murder, armed robbery and assault, and an increase in gang-related gun murders, some in populated and public areas. Avoid isolated areas and beaches after dark and take care at street and beach parties. The natural risks are the June-to-November hurricane season and the La Soufrière volcano, which last erupted in 2021.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November, and that even small tropical storms can quickly become major hurricanes.

Canada's travel advice says La Soufrière is an active volcano whose last significant eruption was in April 2021, and that it has limited police presence around La Soufrière and the north of the island. It advises caution if trekking there.

If you want to stay beyond the period stamped in your passport, apply at the Immigration Head Office in Kingstown, or at the Bequia, Mustique, Canouan or Union Island ports. It costs EC$75 cash per month or part of a month, and the UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to stay longer than the period allowed.

Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted, and the UK government says taxi fares can often be paid in US dollars. It adds that taxis are not metered and to agree the fare with the driver before you set off.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Visitors from the UK, the US and the Schengen countries are granted up to six months on arrival, and most other visa-free nationalities up to three months. CARICOM nationals are granted up to six months and OECS nationals an indefinite stay. Nationals of Afghanistan, Cameroon, China, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Nigeria and Syria must apply to the Ministry of National Security for an entry visa before traveling (EC$200).

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?
faq.answer: The immigration officer grants a visitor's permit on arrival: up to six months for UK, US, Schengen and CARICOM nationals, and up to three months for other nationalities. To stay longer, apply for an extension at the Immigration Head Office in Kingstown or at the Bequia, Mustique, Canouan or Union Island ports; it costs EC$75 cash per month or part of a month.

faq.question: What applies to CARICOM citizens?
faq.answer: The Ministry of National Security says CARICOM nationals are granted an entry permit of up to six months on arrival and OECS nationals an indefinite stay, and that CARICOM citizens holding a CSME certificate issued in their own country may work for six months pending an upgraded certificate from the Ministry.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate?
faq.answer: Only if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow fever transmission risk, according to the UK Foreign Office; WHO's country list sets the requirement for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from such countries.
